name: cmdn-window-slot
description:
The Cmd+N leg. intercept_for answers IDC_NEW_WINDOW with CommandIntercept::NewWindowSlot (rust/atrium-core/src/commands.rs), and the alternative is not a cosmetic difference: falling through reaches OpenEmptyWindow, which hands the factory-created Browser NO controller. That happened once: the gate needed the deleted dylib's spaces group, so Cmd+N silently produced unwired windows.

The suite already PRESSES Cmd+N in two places and grades it in neither. quit-two-windows presses it as the setup for a two-window quit and asserts only the palette line and the quit; dock-reopen-window-counts asserts 'Atrium: RegisterHostInSlot', which nothing logs, so it is marked cannot_pass. Neither can tell a wired slot from a stock window, which is exactly the decision the core makes.

The gate here is the line CreateWindowSlot itself writes (atrium_browser_controller.cc:539). It is worth naming precisely, because dock-reopen-window-counts' cannot_pass prose states this string 'never existed in the tree' and names atrium_browser_controller.mm:538 as the phantom. It does exist, at .cc:539, and it fired on the deployed build during this lane's quit-two-windows run: 'Atrium: Cmd+N opened window-slot 1 for host 0xb3e569340'. The VLOG has two branches off the same statement - 'open_window_slot ... at <point>' when a drop point is supplied, plain 'Cmd+N' when none is. Matching the Cmd+N branch specifically is what keeps this from also matching a drag-out.

Setup is quit-two-windows' opening moves verbatim, including the click at 900,660 rather than an activate: this fixture auto-opens the palette, Escape alone is unreliable at dismissing it, and the click both dismisses and focuses. That sequence is proven to deliver Cmd+N on this build.

actions.note: let the empty space render; the palette auto-opens here
first dismiss attempt - unreliable on its own, which is why the click follows
dismiss the palette for real and put key focus on the browser window, so the chord below is delivered to it
THE MEASUREMENT: IDC_NEW_WINDOW, which intercept_for answers with NewWindowSlot
let the slot be created and its window presented

CreateWindowSlot's post-show hook auto-opens the palette on the NEW slot - the run log shows 'command bar widget showing' 7ms after the window-slot line. Left up, it adds a full-window AXUnknown scrim and the count below reads 3. Dismissing it is not softening the count; it removes a named confounder so the count is two real windows and nothing else
the same belt-and-braces dismiss the opening sequence needs, for the same reason: Escape alone is unreliable on this fixture

assertions.label: wired-slot-not-stock-window
assertions.pattern: Atrium: Cmd\+N opened window-slot [0-9]+ for host
assertions.note: THE GATE, and the whole reason this scenario exists apart from quit-two-windows. CreateWindowSlot writes this line; OpenEmptyWindow writes nothing. So a build that loses the NewWindowSlot intercept still opens a second window and still passes the count below - it just opens an unwired one, and only this line can tell. The 'Cmd\+N' prefix rather than a wildcard pins the no-drop-point branch of the VLOG at atrium_browser_controller.cc:539; the other branch reads 'open_window_slot ... at <point>' and belongs to a drag-out.

assertions.label: cmdn-still-opens-zero-tabs
assertions.note: REGRESSION GUARD. CreateLittleWindow's invalid-seed-URL branch is fixed, but CreateWindowSlot was left alone: it still passes an explicit empty string literal for startup_url, so the ctor's `if (!startup_url.empty())` branch should keep seeing empty from THIS caller and add no tab, same as before the fix. Not a vacuous absence, since an absence assertion needs something positive in front of it: the gate above already proves CreateWindowSlot (not OpenEmptyWindow) is what ran, and empty-window-quit.spaces.json starts the startup window completely tabless with no other path in this scenario that would add one - so if this line ever appeared, it could only be the new slot Cmd+N just opened growing a tab it should not have.

assertions.desc: and the slot really produced a second real window, not just a log line
assertions.note: The effect, asserted separately from the mechanism above so neither can carry the other. A line written by a slot that then failed to present would pass the gate and fail here. Counted only after the new slot's auto-opened palette is dismissed - see the action note; with it up the same run reads 3, the extra being an AXUnknown at the new window's exact bounds.

assertions.desc: Cmd+Q quits with two windows open, through the app's own path
